classifiedFindings.title: setRoute requires only swap_type != 0 on executed hops; Router NG v1.1 dispatches 1..8 and reverts 'Bad swap type' otherwise, so a swap_type >= 9 route is stored as valid and reverts every harvest that sells that token
classifiedFindings.proposedSeverityUpstream: QA (code-scan qa; profile local-low; patterns potential-low; all agree fail-loud)
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessNote: story-007 Goal sentence overclaims what its spec block validates; recorded as cross-reference on this row only (no separate F, no double count).

classification.assetImpact: None. Availability only: every harvest that delivers the affected strategy token reverts Error('Bad swap type') until the owner re-sets the route or callers exempt the strategy. Atomic revert; forge+medusa invariants show harvester and caller balances unchanged; nothing stranded.
attackPath: 1. Precondition (owner footgun, not an attack): owner registers a route whose executed hop has swap_type >= 9, e.g. copied from tooling targeting Router NG v1.2 (9 = ERC4626) or a mis-entered field.
2. setRoute accepts it: executed-hop check is presence (swap_type != 0), not the immutable v1.1 router's range 1..8; the new 'params consistent with path' validation reads as having vetted it.
3. Test suite cannot catch it: MockCurveRouter executes swap_type >= 9.
4. Any harvest() including that strategy reverts inside router.exchange with 'Bad swap type'; harvest.sh's eth_call simulation surfaces the Error(string), so no gas is burnt on-chain.
5. Recovery: one owner setRoute call, or callers exempt the strategy meanwhile.
classification.likelihood: low - requires an owner route slip of a specific shape; contract not yet deployed
classification.assumptions: Non-malicious owner; immutable router is Curve Router NG v1.1 (dispatches 1..8).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner misconfiguration; strategy holding that token included in a harvest.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low, not QA: a real, reachable function impact (one strategy's harvests blocked) behind a validator that creates false confidence and a mock that hides it, i.e. a mild non-obvious footgun of the same class as L-03 (Low). Not Medium: fail-loud, atomic, zero value at risk, simulated before broadcast, fixed by one owner call. Distinct from M-01 (silent strand) and not an incomplete fix of it.
classifiedFindings.borderlineNote: Low vs QA. Floor is QA (fail-loud on an attended owner path is not a defect per se; all upstream agents proposed QA). Chose Low because harvest() is public and the denial reaches third-party callers, and the validation advertised by story-007 is what lets it through. Severity-auditor may downgrade to QA without loss of recall; ceiling is Low.
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Until fixed: only register swap_type values 1..8 for the v1.1 router; eth_call router.exchange (or a harvest simulation) with the stored route before relying on it. Fix: bound executed swap_type to 1..8 in setRoute and make MockCurveRouter revert outside 1..8.

classifiedFindings.title: story-006 premise that a k=0 route 'delivers path[0]' is false for Router NG v1.1 (hop 0 always executes); InvalidRouteEnd @dev, ICurveRouterNG NatSpec and two test comments inherit it

classification.assetImpact: None. Accept/reject set of setRoute unaffected; the only reachable consequence (stale k=0 reward-token route after setRewardToken) is fail-loud and already tracked under L-03.

classifiedFindings.justification: Story/NatSpec premise is factually wrong (Router NG v1.1 always executes hop 0, so k=0 never 'delivers path[0]') but code behaviour is unchanged; Law-2 spec-conformance item at Info, not QA-bundle noise.

classifiedFindings.title: story-007 premise that _pools[i] is used by zap swap types 3/5/7 is false; deployed Router NG v1.1 reads pools only for swap_type 3; ICurveRouterNG NatSpec copies it

classification.assetImpact: None. Executed-hop pools are unconstrained and the router reads them only for swap_type 3, so behaviour is correct; risk is only that a future validator built on the '3/5/7' premise would be wrong.

classifiedFindings.justification: Documentation/story premise error (pools used by 3/5/7 vs only 3 in deployed v1.1) with no behavioural effect; Info spec-conformance, kept separate from F-06 (different story, different false statement).

classifiedFindings.title: story-001 (terminal, unamended) still prescribes the last-non-zero route rule and the vulnerable CurveAMMAdapter template that stories 006/007 supersede; supersession is recorded only in a 006 Concerns bullet

splitFrom.why: Run-01 merged F-02 into DEDUP-001 (= M-01). Its Law-1 half closes with M-01; its Law-2 half (story-001 still prescribes the last-non-zero rule and names the still-vulnerable vault CurveAMMAdapter template) survives. Keeping it under M-01's fingerprint would block proposing M-01 fixed or hide the residual; a distinct rootCauseClass keeps both honest.

classifiedFindings.labelNote: Do not reuse F-02 (run-01 tag bound to M-01); new identity because rootCauseClass differs.

classification.assetImpact: None at 6b862aa: code conforms to superseding stories 006/007. Residual is regression-by-re-derivation: anyone (human or agent) implementing or grading against story-001 would re-introduce M-01, and story-001 still points at the still-vulnerable vault CurveAMMAdapter template.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a future re-implementation or review against the stale story
classification.assumptions: Later story governs where stories conflict.

classifiedFindings.justification: Law-2 spec conflict between a terminal, unamended story and the code that follows its superseding stories; no live impact, so QA-level, routed to spec-conformance (not the QA bundle). Split from M-01 so M-01 can be proposed fixed without hiding this residual.
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Product owner: annotate story-001 (L34/L130/L133) 'Superseded by story-006/007', or record an explicit no-amend policy for terminal stories. Rescan check next run.
